captions.text:
TeamChat AI on the deployed stack: Firebase Hosting → Cloud Run API → Cloud Tasks → worker → Vertex Gemini → Cloud SQL.
Source d66da3d · API teamchat-api-00016-ct7 · worker teamchat-worker-00016-24v. Two Northside buyers sign in (passwords masked; account emails blurred by the recording).
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Real-time: one WebSocket per browser, no polling. The left buyer's message appears on the right as it is saved.
Known limits shown as-is: senders appear as Firebase user IDs, and the recording script scrolls each transcript (no auto-scroll yet).
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Native function calling: Gemini calls search_catalog itself. Both screens show the fetched rows while the answer is built.
Every catalog code and margin class shown comes from the supplied catalog, not from the model.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Retail math: calculate_uplift computes the coefficient score on the server and lists superseded classes (1003, 506).
ST-4003 already carries class 318 via APP-100.11, so APP-100.12 adds no new class: difference 0. No money figure is invented.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Honesty: beekeeping veils are not in the supplied catalog. search_catalog finds no match, and the answer says so.
No code is invented: catalog codes can only reach the screen from a fetched row.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Shared memory: a paraphrased question finds a decision recorded in another room (pgvector, 768-dimension embeddings),
with its author and date.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Tenant isolation: ST-4013 belongs to Valley Home Goods. Postgres row-level security returns nothing to Northside,
the same answer as for a store that does not exist.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Prompt injection: the admin-mode line changes nothing. Every tool runs with the tenant the server verified
from the Firebase token, inside Postgres row-level security, so there is no other chain's data to reveal.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
Refresh mid-answer: the left buyer asks a two-part question, and the right window reloads
as soon as the first fetch appears, while the answer is still being built.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
After the reload the right window replays the whole turn from the server:
every fetched result and the answer, in order, once each.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text: Reconnect: the right window goes offline while the left buyer keeps posting.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text: Back online: the right window replays from its saved cursor. Both missed messages arrive once each, in order.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning

captions.text:
The other chain: the right window signs out and signs in as a Valley Home Goods buyer.
ST-4013 is Valley's own store, so Valley gets its assortment: the same store Northside was told does not exist.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · #supply-planning · RIGHT: VALLEY BUYER 1 · #range-planning

captions.text:
Every claim in this video is also checked automatically against the deployed stack.
Results, raw WebSocket frames and database comparisons: qa_evidence/runs in the repository.
captions.cast: LEFT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 1 · RIGHT: NORTHSIDE BUYER 2 · #supply-planning
